/-!
# Erdős Problem 196

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/196](https://www.erdosproblems.com/196)
-/
namespace Erdos196

/-- Must every permutation of $\mathbb{N}$, contain a monotone 4-term arithmetic progression?-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_196 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (f : ℕ ≃ ℕ), HasMonotoneAP f 4 := by
  sorry

end Erdos196

reformulations.difference: The list-based AP helper does not explicitly require a nonzero common difference and represents decreasing progressions by reversing a progression with natural-number difference.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a permutation, strictly increasing indices have distinct images. A zero difference would make all four images equal, so the difference is necessarily positive. Unfolding the helpers gives exactly four indices i < j < k < m whose values are a, a+d, a+2d, a+3d, or the reverse, with d > 0. This equivalence was proved as explicit_iff in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses naturals including zero, whereas the primary literature formulates the problem for positive integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Translating every value by one bijectively transports permutations of the naturals to enumerations of the positive integers and preserves arithmetic progressions in either direction. Subtracting one provides the inverse transport; changing the starting index from zero to one preserves index order. The equivalence between the universally quantified natural-number version and the positive-integer enumeration version was proved as positive_integer_version_iff.
